html:
The Maia, written Maya on the map, were an Aboriginal Australian people of the Gascoyne region of Western Australia, near the coast north of Shark Bay. The map shows them only in 1815.

Very little is recorded of them beyond their name and territory, and the group is obscure even in specialist sources. Neighbours on the map include the Yinggarda, the Tharrgari and the Payungu. Dutch ships, including that of Dirk Hartog in 1616, had touched this coast long before, but settlers did not arrive until pastoral stations spread north in the 1870s and 1880s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
